meta.title: Ocean Plastic Mining Project
meta.description: An open engineering project to reduce the cost of permanently removing ocean plastic. Inspect the model. Challenge the assumptions.

ui.reviewNote: Initial translations are open for community correction. No human review is claimed.
ui.footer: Measure it. Test it. Lower the cost.
ui.modelOnly: Model only — your inputs are not verified data.
ui.invalid: Enter finite, non-negative costs and revenues, a lifetime above zero, a discount rate from 0 to 100%, and verified tonnes above zero. Complete every field.
ui.inputHint: All inputs are annual EUR except initial CAPEX, asset life, discount rate and tonnes. Enter 0 for a known zero; blank means unknown.
ui.outputHint: Gross LCOCR does not subtract revenue or public payments. No default scenario is presented as real performance.

home.title: Can we make ocean cleanup
home.subtitle: Reduce the cost of permanent plastic removal until many independent teams can take part. Start with an inspectable model, not a promise.
home.northText: Cost per tonne permanently removed. Full lifecycle. Inspectable evidence.
home.milestone: A cost curve, not a countdown.
home.miningQuestion: How low can extraction cost go?
home.metaphor: “Mining” is an economic and engineering metaphor. It does not imply that ocean plastic is profitable, or that pyrolysis is the right route.
home.pioneersText: The Ocean Cleanup has carried out substantial engineering exploration of offshore plastic collection. Can the full cost now fall far enough for independent teams to replicate the work?
home.analogy: NASA → SpaceX is a strategic analogy: early exploration, then industrialization, standardization and reuse. It is not evidence that ocean cleanup will follow the same path.
home.frontier: The next frontier is discovering how cheaply plastic can be removed permanently.
home.challengeText: Bring a calculation, a dataset, a test — or a well-supported objection.
home.principle: Extraordinary engineering claims require inspectable evidence.
home.principleText: Our core assumptions can be wrong. Failed experiments and negative results belong in the record.
home.breakText: Find an error. Submit evidence. Improve the model. Build an independent experiment.
home.last: The ocean doesn’t need another promise. It needs a measurable cost curve.

thesis.title: The thesis is a question.
thesis.intro: Can automation, standardization, energy recovery and shared logistics reduce full cost enough for independent teams to participate?
sections: Start with the denominator
The goal is permanent removal, not collection alone. Losses, rejected material and unverified end destinations do not count as permanently removed tonnes.
Test the economic transition
Public funding may start experiments. Independent teams may enter; shared services may emerge. Each arrow is a hypothesis, not a forecast.
An open infrastructure
Publish assumptions, models, evidence and failed tests so that other teams can compare approaches and maintain the project independently of its founder.
A resource with an unknown grade
Offshore plastic is dispersed, heterogeneous and contaminated. A total garbage-patch mass cannot substitute for a workable density distribution or a measured collection rate.

cost.title: The cost is the challenge.
cost.intro: The north-star metric is cost per tonne permanently removed. Vessel size, collector length, publicity and fundraising are not substitutes.
sections: One complete boundary
Annualized capital plus all annual operating, search, energy, logistics, maintenance, processing, disposal and compliance costs, divided by verified permanent removal.
No verified baseline yet
The curve below is conceptual. It has no dates or numeric cost axis and does not estimate any existing organization’s cost.

challenges.title: Open engineering challenges.
challenges.intro: Ten bounded questions. Comparable metrics. No preferred technology. Every challenge starts at hypothesis level.

evidence.title: Show the evidence.
evidence.intro: Evidence quality and conclusion direction are separate axes. E5 can support or reject a hypothesis. An E0 claim is still a hypothesis.
sections: A core project assumption was wrong.
This statement must be publishable when evidence warrants it. No core assumption has yet been reliably rejected in this project; the rejected record is currently empty.
Report failures
Record null results, adverse effects, losses and conflicting evidence. Retain earlier claims and explain revisions instead of silently removing inconvenient results.

solutions.title: Let evidence and cost decide.
solutions.intro: Competing approaches are welcome. These are research directions, not operating teams or validated systems.

leaderboard.title: A leaderboard that earns its numbers.
leaderboard.intro: No solution has met the verification threshold yet.
sections: Admission threshold

Draft V1 requires E5 or E6 evidence, inspectable cost boundaries, traceable dry mass and final fate, test duration, location, and independent audit of the submission. E5 is not independent replication.
Compare like with like
Separate evidence tiers. Report uncertainty, price year and operating conditions. An E1 estimate must never compete as an equal to an E5 operational result.

starter-kit.title: Start with something inspectable.
starter-kit.intro: Download working templates. Replace unknowns with evidence. Hardware designs and deployment protocols are not available yet.

contribute.title: How do you want to contribute?
contribute.intro: A correction can be more useful than an endorsement. Start with a bounded question and enough evidence for someone else to check it.

methodology.title: Define the boundary. Then measure.
methodology.intro: LCOCR — Levelized Cost of Ocean Cleanup and Recovery. Version 0.1 is a proposal awaiting RFC review, not a frozen standard.
sections: Permanent removal

Use verified dry plastic mass with a documented chain of custody and final treatment or disposal. Subtract losses and any material returned to the environment. Energy recovery is not permanent carbon storage; emissions and residues must be reported separately.
Avoid double counting

OPEX is residual operating expenditure only. Search, energy, logistics, maintenance, processing, disposal and compliance each have their own mutually exclusive bucket. Keep a ledger for allocation and shared assets.
Capital and uncertainty

Annualize capital with a capital-recovery factor. Declare life, discount rate, currency price year, utilization, allocation, measurement error and sensitivity ranges. A blank value is unknown, never zero.
T1 has two boundaries

The operating threshold is resource revenue plus public payment ≥ full operating cost. The homepage uses the more conservative full-cost condition including capital replacement. Report both; operating survival alone does not prove durable viability.
T2: subsidy exit
Resource revenue ≥ full cost, including annualized capital, compliant processing, disposal and risk allowances. This remains an unverified research threshold.
T3: distant research
Long-term offshore living cost < shore living + crew rotation + transport cost. This is not a V1 deployment objective or a forecast.

governance.title: Built to outlive its founder.
governance.intro: Stewardship follows sustained, reliable contribution. The founder has no permanent right to supreme maintenance authority.
sections: Founder / Steward
Initially coordinates project direction, proposed methodology and community formation. Can later move into an advisory role without blocking succession.
Domain maintainers
Marine engineering, energy and pyrolysis, remote sensing, cost model, data, web and translation each need accountable maintainers. All roles are currently unassigned.
Lead Maintainer and succession

When a maintainer group exists, candidates are nominated publicly with contribution evidence. After a 14-day discussion, a two-thirds vote of active maintainers selects a lead. Inactivity and conflicts of interest have documented procedures.
RFC decisions

Changes to LCOCR, evidence levels, challenge evaluation, data boundaries, governance, licenses or major technical standards require a public RFC and recorded decision. RFC-0001 is proposed, not accepted.

about.title: An open question. A public record.
about.intro: Ocean Plastic Mining Project is a working name for open engineering research. Project status: research / pre-validation.
sections: What this project is not

Not a fundraising campaign; not a cleanup company; not a floating-city promotion; not a proven profitable business; not a mandate to pyrolyze all plastic; not opposition to existing ocean organizations; not a conclusion looking for evidence.
Safety and responsibility

Marine work, vessels, machinery, autonomous equipment, fuels and high-temperature processing require competent review. Public discussion or designs are not permission to deploy. Experiments must meet applicable maritime, environmental, class, equipment and impact requirements.
Privacy and openness

No accounts, payments or cross-site tracking. Language is stored locally. Optional visitor counting stores hashes of random browser IDs and a first-party cookie, not IP addresses or browsing paths. Code: Apache-2.0; original content: CC BY 4.0; third-party licenses remain unchanged.

CH-001.title: Ocean Plastic Density
CH-001.summary: How many kilograms can a workable area yield per square kilometre, navigation hour and effective capture hour?
CH-001.problem: How many kilograms can a workable area yield per square kilometre, navigation hour and effective capture hour?
CH-001.whyItMatters: A density distribution, not a garbage-patch total, must feed the cost model.
assumptions: Accessible density may differ from published regional averages.
openQuestions: How do season, weather, depth and capture selectivity change usable density?

CH-002.title: Logistics Energy Floor
CH-002.summary: What minimum energy is needed to move, capture, store and transport a tonne, even if plastic arrives beside the collector for free?
CH-002.problem: What minimum energy is needed to move, capture, store and transport a tonne, even if plastic arrives beside the collector for free?
CH-002.whyItMatters: Find the physical floor that smarter software cannot remove.
assumptions: Transfers, station keeping and return trips may dominate energy use.
openQuestions: Which lower bounds remain valid under realistic waves and utilization?

CH-003.title: Low-Cost Autonomous Interceptor
CH-003.summary: Design an unmanned or highly automated unit for the lowest complete lifecycle cost per tonne permanently removed.
CH-003.problem: Design an unmanned or highly automated unit for the lowest complete lifecycle cost per tonne permanently removed.
CH-003.whyItMatters: Maximum capture alone does not establish a cheaper system.
assumptions: Autonomy may reduce crew expense while increasing recovery and maintenance cost.
openQuestions: What failure rate and service interval make the full system competitive?

CH-004.title: Satellite Plastic Detection
CH-004.summary: At what resolution, weather conditions and confidence can satellite sensing reduce unproductive searching?
CH-004.problem: At what resolution, weather conditions and confidence can satellite sensing reduce unproductive searching?
CH-004.whyItMatters: Separate theoretical possibility, laboratory research, commercial data and verified sea operations.
assumptions: A detectable surface signal may not identify collectable plastic.
openQuestions: What are precision, recall, revisit interval and cost per avoided search hour?

CH-005.title: Drone Local Search
CH-005.summary: Can drones scout around a support ship or interceptor to reduce search energy and time per captured tonne?
CH-005.problem: Can drones scout around a support ship or interceptor to reduce search energy and time per captured tonne?
CH-005.whyItMatters: Measure net savings after flights, recovery and data processing.
assumptions: Local reconnaissance may improve routing only in limited conditions.
openQuestions: What range, weather window and false-positive rate are operationally useful?

CH-006.title: Interception Drag
CH-006.summary: How much drag do interception systems create at real current speeds and sea states?
CH-006.problem: How much drag do interception systems create at real current speeds and sea states?
CH-006.whyItMatters: Connect structure directly to propulsion power, fuel demand and €/t.
assumptions: Controlled-water measurements may not generalize to loaded offshore systems.
openQuestions: How do loading, waves, fouling and geometry change the force curve?

CH-007.title: Pyrolysis Net Energy
CH-007.summary: How much usable net energy remains after treating real aged, contaminated, salty and wet ocean plastic?
CH-007.problem: How much usable net energy remains after treating real aged, contaminated, salty and wet ocean plastic?
CH-007.whyItMatters: Include drying, sorting, preheating, reaction, cleanup, auxiliaries, residue handling and maintenance downtime.
assumptions: Ideal-polymer heating value may greatly overstate useful net energy.
openQuestions: Can a measured mass-and-energy balance include emissions, residues and actual plant availability?

CH-008.title: Mothership + Swarm
CH-008.summary: Does one shared support vessel with many inexpensive interceptors lower €/t relative to a single large system?
CH-008.problem: Does one shared support vessel with many inexpensive interceptors lower €/t relative to a single large system?
CH-008.whyItMatters: Compare 1, 10, 50 and 100 units under identical boundaries.
assumptions: Shared support savings may be offset by coordination and service bottlenecks.
openQuestions: How do queuing, correlated failures and weather affect utilization?

CH-009.title: Offshore Maintenance Economy
CH-009.summary: What happens to cost when 1, 10, 100 or 1000 teams share repair, supplies, storage, crew transport, processing and data?
CH-009.problem: What happens to cost when 1, 10, 100 or 1000 teams share repair, supplies, storage, crew transport, processing and data?
CH-009.whyItMatters: Validate economies of scale instead of assuming they exist.
assumptions: Growing demand may support shared services but can also increase congestion.
openQuestions: What demand, distance and service reliability are needed to break even?

CH-010.title: LCOCR Baseline
CH-010.summary: Establish a complete and inspectable Levelized Cost of Ocean Cleanup and Recovery baseline.
CH-010.problem: Establish a complete and inspectable Levelized Cost of Ocean Cleanup and Recovery baseline.
CH-010.whyItMatters: Include annualized CAPEX and every operating cost per verified tonne permanently removed.
assumptions: Cost boundaries and removal verification may change apparent performance.
openQuestions: Which missing inputs most affect the result, and can an independent team reproduce it?
